# AGENTS.md

Moneo is a Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app using Supabase/Postgres, Drizzle, Vercel Workflow, Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK via OpenRouter.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.
- For schema changes, add a new ordered migration and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Do not rewrite applied migrations.
- Supabase CLI isn't linked: run it via `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`), e.g. `npx supabase migration repair --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" --status reverted <versions>`.
- for each thing break it down and for each thing make a commit directly if a big task make multiple commits

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app/config/build changes and Playwright for changed user flows. Gated E2E requires configured Supabase/auth; see `e2e/README.md`.

Signed-in E2E uses one persistent QA user (login in the git-ignored `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`). With the app on localhost:3000:

- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` signs it in and writes `e2e/.auth.json` (creates the user on first run).
- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset` empties its workspace; do this before a full suite run. Never delete the user.

## Context
 
 
Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, and `e2e/README.md` for browser-test setup.


# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

- [lib workflow tests need OPENAI key](lib-workflow-tests-need-openai-key.md) — 14 lib/ tests fail on main without OPENAI_API_KEY
- [Python edits need UTF-8](python-edits-need-utf8.md) — open() is cp1252 here; non-ASCII gets corrupted
- [AI keys for dev](qa-chat-needs-openrouter-model.md) — OpenRouter out of credits 2026-10-27; OpenAI key (gpt-live-1) in main and voice worktree .env since 2026-10-30
- [Cash balance default account](cash-balance-default-account.md) — stated cash goes to the currency's cash account; create or ask when none or several
- [Voice feature branch workflow](voice-feature-branch-workflow.md) — PRs go into t3/voice-finance-agent; user opens final PR to main; ignore Entire gate
- [Voice design decisions](voice-design-decisions.md) — GPT-Live hands off to /api/chat, parallel tasks without a limit, tap-only cards, one mic with Send/Done
- [Overnight autonomy and subagent models](overnight-autonomy-and-subagent-models.md) — decide with my recommendation and report later; subagents use Opus 5.5 low or Sonnet 5.5; test voice against the real API
- [Perf measurement setup](perf-measurement-setup.md) — measure on a prod build with a seeded QA workspace; React cache() is a no-op in route handlers

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is a Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app using Supabase/Postgres, Drizzle, Vercel Workflow, Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK via OpenRouter.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.
- For schema changes, add a new ordered migration and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Do not rewrite applied migrations.
- Supabase CLI isn't linked: run it via `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`), e.g. `npx supabase migration repair --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" --status reverted <versions>`.
- for each thing break it down and for each thing make a commit directly if a big task make multiple commits

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app/config/build changes and Playwright for changed user flows. Gated E2E requires configured Supabase/auth; see `e2e/README.md`.

Signed-in E2E uses one persistent QA user (login in the git-ignored `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`). With the app on localhost:3000:

- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` signs it in and writes `e2e/.auth.json` (creates the user on first run).
- `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset` empties its workspace; do this before a full suite run. Never delete the user.

## Context
 
 
Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, and `e2e/README.md` for browser-test setup.


# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

- [lib workflow tests need OPENAI key](lib-workflow-tests-need-openai-key.md) — 14 lib/ tests fail on main without OPENAI_API_KEY
- [Python edits need UTF-8](python-edits-need-utf8.md) — open() is cp1252 here; non-ASCII gets corrupted
- [AI keys for dev](qa-chat-needs-openrouter-model.md) — OpenRouter out of credits 2026-10-27; OpenAI key (gpt-live-1) in main and voice worktree .env since 2026-10-30
- [Cash balance default account](cash-balance-default-account.md) — stated cash goes to the currency's cash account; create or ask when none or several
- [Voice feature branch workflow](voice-feature-branch-workflow.md) — PRs go into t3/voice-finance-agent; user opens final PR to main; ignore Entire gate

</pull_request_linking>

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours, and it finishes in this turn (Claude `Agent` always with `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), background work, or `delegate_task` by name. A native type running another provider's model counts too. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` to a T3 tool to act there. Ids are then that machine's, so pass `threadId`.
- A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` to verify or show your own edit, even a frontend edit or an open tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Use them only when the current request asks for browser work or names a page or tab. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.


### Background work you wait on

To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call `t3_background_wait` with its task ID before you end your turn. Do not mark work you leave running, or PRs. T3 MCP tools are deferred: load one with ToolSearch before you call it.

## T3 Code devices

When a task needs an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator, on this machine or on an SSH device host such as a remote Mac, use the device tools so the user can watch it in the Device panel. Load them with ToolSearch `select:mcp__t3-code__device_list,mcp__t3-code__device_open,mcp__t3-code__device_screenshot,mcp__t3-code__device_close`.
1. Call `device_list` unless you already have the device's `hostId` and `id`.
2. Call `device_open` with both. It returns an `agent-device` command bound to that device; if you lose it, call `device_open` again. Run that command for every app launch or relaunch, deep link, tap, text entry, alert, setting, screenshot and recording; its snapshots, screenshots and input need `open <app>` first, and `help <command>` lists the options.
3. Call `device_screenshot` to look at the screen.

Never do those with `xcrun simctl`, `idb`, `adb`, ssh, or scripts that wrap them. ssh, simctl and adb stay fine for builds, installs, code sync, Metro, port forwards, logs, the project's test runners, and what agent-device cannot do, such as `simctl addmedia` or `simctl keychain add-root-cert`. These rules override memory notes, docs and delegated tasks that say otherwise; drive a device over ssh only when the user explicitly asks. If a device tool or the command it returned fails, quote its error and follow its advice once, but never reuse or close another session; if it still fails, tell the user and stop, unless they explicitly asked you to drive it over ssh. If the platform you need is unavailable, say so. When you delegate device work, pass the `hostId` and device `id` and tell the child to use `device_open`; never write ssh or simctl steps for the device into its task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` to a T3 tool to act there. Ids are then that machine's, so pass `threadId`.
- A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` to verify or show your own edit, even a frontend edit or an open tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Use them only when the current request asks for browser work or names a page or tab. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.


### Background work you wait on

To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call `t3_background_wait` with its task ID before you end your turn. Do not mark work you leave running, or PRs. T3 MCP tools are deferred: load one with ToolSearch before you call it.

## T3 Code devices

When a task needs an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator, on this machine or on an SSH device host such as a remote Mac, use the device tools so the user can watch it in the Device panel. Load them with ToolSearch `select:mcp__t3-code__device_list,mcp__t3-code__device_open,mcp__t3-code__device_screenshot,mcp__t3-code__device_close`.
1. Call `device_list` unless you already have the device's `hostId` and `id`.
2. Call `device_open` with both. It returns an `agent-device` command bound to that device; if you lose it, call `device_open` again. Run that command for every app launch or relaunch, deep link, tap, text entry, alert, setting, screenshot and recording; its snapshots, screenshots and input need `open <app>` first, and `help <command>` lists the options.
3. Call `device_screenshot` to look at the screen.

Never do those with `xcrun simctl`, `idb`, `adb`, ssh, or scripts that wrap them. ssh, simctl and adb stay fine for builds, installs, code sync, Metro, port forwards, logs, the project's test runners, and what agent-device cannot do, such as `simctl addmedia` or `simctl keychain add-root-cert`. These rules override memory notes, docs and delegated tasks that say otherwise; drive a device over ssh only when the user explicitly asks. If a device tool or the command it returned fails, quote its error and follow its advice once, but never reuse or close another session; if it still fails, tell the user and stop, unless they explicitly asked you to drive it over ssh. If the platform you need is unavailable, say so. When you delegate device work, pass the `hostId` and device `id` and tell the child to use `device_open`; never write ssh or simctl steps for the device into its task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.thinking:
I'm tracing through the cancel logic: canceling sets status, patches the record, and aborts the fetch, which should be caught cleanly in run(). But I'm wondering whether there's a race where cancel doesn't actually remove a result that already arrived and got queued before the cancel took effect.

I think I've found a real bug: controller.cancel doesn't clear unclaimedTask or announced state, and more importantly, the stream keeps emitting step/thinking events after cancellation, so those handlers overwrite the "stopped" status with new step text unless they explicitly check for canceled state first.

I'm also checking the replace-task flow — when task B cancels task A via call_replace_task, A's run() should bail out on the canceled status check, but I need to verify whether A's cards, if already generated, still leak into the tasks array before that check happens.

There's an edge case where A finishes between B's session start and B's tool call, so A is "done" with its result queued or being spoken when the replace fires — the server's replaced() filter removes it from outbox but doesn't clear A's cards from the UI, so I should set cards to empty on replace to avoid showing rejected card content. There's also a minor regex edge case in the "latest running task" restriction where words like "too" could ambiguously match continuation phrases. Finally, I'm noting that steering input exists in chat via take_chat_steers but isn't wired into the update-query call, which users would expect for "update your search" type requests.

On flush(), the recursive scheduling after handoff works correctly since resultSaid() returns false right after current is set. The claimUnheard scheduling on every transcript delta creates many cheap timers, which is fine though slightly wasteful. In claim(), if words are empty it retries after a delay, which seems safe even if another delegation arrives in between.

I'm spotting a real bug: when a user types a message while the voice channel is still connecting, the send silently fails if the channel isn't open by delivery time, so the result gets dropped from voice (though it still shows in the chat UI) — the outbox entry is consumed without actually transmitting.

The simplest fix is restricting typing to only when the connection is fully live rather than merely "open" (which includes connecting), so I'll change the condition that controls when the form is shown.

For cut-off detection, transcripts arrive about a second late, so interruptions get detected with some delay, and resultSaid() depends on mic-quiet metering that's already been tuned — I'll leave that logic alone. There's a design tradeoff where if the user interrupts with a new request, that result waits until resume() fires, which seems intentional, but I'm now wondering whether an explicit "stop" or "skip that" interruption should still trigger the normal resume flow or needs special handling.

Looking at the useState hook that instantiates VoiceCallController with a captured conversationId, I'm checking whether the effect's dependency on conversationId could leave the controller stale if that ID ever changes without a full remount.

For cancel(), the PATCH retries on 404 up to ten times while abort happens after the loop; aborting the fetch early mostly matters if the POST hasn't reached the server yet, otherwise the server run continues via after() regardless—so I'll just have the controller ignore any events that arrive after cancellation rather than trying to perfectly sequence the abort and retry.

On hang-up mid-task, saveRecord sends tasks that keep running server-side since fetches aren't aborted on unmount; the controller just sends no-ops and clears onAnswer, which seems fine. I'm also noting that in React StrictMode dev, double effect execution closes and reopens the peer connection, but since startedAt is still null at the first cleanup this shouldn't cause issues, though controller state like captions persists across remounts which I should verify is intentional. I'm also wondering whether any `error` event from the server permanently marks the controller as errored even for non-fatal cases, like sending a commentary append with a null delegation_id — I should check the real API behavior and look at the voice-call-check script to verify this assumption.

Now I realize the error banner never gets cleared once set, which could be a problem. I also need to check whether delegationId can be null for typed tasks when building the stillWorking payload, and whether the check script actually tests that null case.

content.thinking:
No errors there. For interruptions during voice, the cut/resume logic already exists and was tested before, so I'll trust it given the limited budget but still flag it. One thing worth noting as over-engineered: the claimTakenOn/claimUnheard logic with regex heuristics trying to guess requests that weren't explicitly delegated feels overly complex.

Looking closer, that heuristic matches real model behavior and removing it risks regressions, so I'll report it rather than rip it out. The cancel retry loop of up to ten PATCH attempts exists because cancellation can race with claiming, so that should stay too. The watchSlow and followUp mechanisms both handle announcing still-running tasks, which seems like duplication but is probably fine as-is.

Now I'm implementing the cancel function in the controller — filtering it out of the outbox, clearing the cut reference if it matches, and updating the status to canceled. I'm second-guessing whether clearing the cards array makes sense here, since those cards might still exist as server-side proposals even after the user stops the task.

Actually proposals persist in the database and surface in chat regardless, so for stopped-but-done tasks I should leave the cards visible rather than clearing them — but for replaced tasks, the server already dismissed those proposals, so clearing is correct there. I want `replaced()` to reuse the same cancel logic, and I'm adding a `queued` getter that combines outbox ids with the cut id into a set, so the UI can show the stop control whenever something is running or queued, while only firing the PATCH if it was actually running. I also need an event guard inside `run()` that bails early if the event isn't a tool event or if the task has already been canceled.

content.thinking: Now I should put together a summary noting the over-engineering issues I found, presenting them as something to report rather than fix, along with the reasoning behind that choice.

content.text:
I tested the call feature against the real API and the core behaviours mostly work. I found four bugs and fixed them in two commits on `t3/03840b08` (`2ec88535`, `9c6558b8`). Unit tests (1202) and lint pass; I didn't run `npm run build`.

**What I tested live** (real GPT-Live and chat model):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/voice-call-check.mjs`: three spoken requests, a card, the typed message, the summary card after hang-up | All 12 checks pass |
| Changing your query ("No wait, leave that, I meant this month") | Works: the old request shows "replaced" and only the new answer is spoken |
| Stopping a running request | Works: it shows "stopped" and nothing is spoken |
| Queueing three requests at once | Works: they run in parallel and are spoken one at a time as they finish |
| Stopping an answered result before it's spoken | Was broken, works now (bug 1) |

**Bugs fixed**
1. **You couldn't stop a result once its answer arrived.** After a request finished, its Stop button disappeared, but the result could sit in the queue for 15 seconds or more and then be spoken anyway. Now Stop stays until the result is handed to the voice, and stopping it drops it from the queue, including the unfinished rest of a result you talked over.
2. **A stopped request could still show progress.** Progress updates that arrived just after you pressed Stop replaced "stopped" with "searching transactions" and were still passed to the voice. They're ignored now.
3. **Cards stayed on screen after a correction.** When a new request replaced an old one, the server dismissed the old request's cards, but the call screen kept showing them. They're removed now.
4. **Typing while the call was connecting lost the answer.** The text box was there before the connection was open, so the answer was never spoken. The box now appears once the call is live.

I added a unit test for bugs 1 and 2. Interrupting by voice and adding another request is handled by existing code that a test covers; I couldn't test it live because the test script can only play a fixed audio file into a fake mic.

**Over-engineering: found but not removed.** Each of these is there to work around something the voice model or a race actually does, so removing it without real spoken tests would bring old bugs back:
- **Word-guessing rules** in `lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts:49-58`, `216-238`. They guess when the voice said "I'm on it" but never handed the request over. This is the most fragile part and only covers English phrasing. If the voice model starts handing requests over reliably, delete it.
- **Many timing constants** in `voice-call-controller.ts:45-73`, each re-checked every 300 ms, to decide whether the voice has finished speaking a result. It works, but it's hard to reason about. A single "finished speaking" event from the API would replace most of it.
- **Two ways of saying "still working"** (one for slow tasks, one after each result). They could be merged into one, but it's a small gain.
- **"Also/too" word check** in `lib/ai/voice-call.ts:42`. It repeats a rule the prompt already gives, but it's a cheap safeguard against wrongly replacing a request, so I left it.

I copied `.env` from the main checkout into this worktree for the live tests, and left a scenario test script at `.qa/call-scenarios.mjs`, which git ignores.

content.thinking:
I need to think through the interruption case carefully: if a user says "stop, next" while a result is being spoken, I should cut it off and resume afterward, but the resume shouldn't just pass through an instruction that risks GPT-Live saying something extra. A cleaner approach might be detecting skip words like "stop/skip/next" deterministically from the cut words rather than relying on an instruction handoff.

I also need to check whether flush waits for Moneo to finish responding to the interruption itself — it probably doesn't, since resultSaid becomes true once current is nulled, so the handoff could overlap with GPT-Live's reply like "okay." That seems acceptable since the commentary queues after anyway.

There's also a timing concern: if the "stop" transcript arrives about a second late, I need to verify resultSaid isn't prematurely marked done, but since the mic stays loud while the user is speaking, it should use the longer RESULT_DONE_MS threshold, so the cut should still register in time. I also want to make sure "stop" phrasing doesn't get misclassified as a request by the heard-detection logic.

I'm now worried GPT-Live could actually delegate "stop, next" as if it were a real chat request, producing a nonsensical answer—so I should guard against that in the claim logic by checking for short skip-command phrases (six words or fewer) before allowing a claim to start.

On simplification, I'm weighing whether to drop both claimTakenOn and claimUnheard entirely in favor of relying on delegation plus leftover words, but that risks small talk bleeding into the next request text. Since the user wants things simpler, I'll remove claimTakenOn as the more heuristic-heavy piece while keeping a lighter version of claimUnheard based on the small-talk/asks regex.

content.thinking:
I'm wondering whether the "month" leftover sticking to the next request is a regression from removing claimTakenOn's earlier guard logic that used to absorb that leftover word during an early hand-off.

Checking the old code, the filtering was actually identical, and tracing through the sequence shows "month" gets prepended to the rent request the same way it did before — so this isn't a regression, it's a pre-existing timing-dependent bug that just happens to surface more often now.

One possible fix: when claiming words, treat a leftover fragment as belonging to the next request only if the gap between it and the previously claimed piece's end is small, since transcript deltas carry start_ms/end_ms we could use to distinguish "still the same sentence" from "a new request." The tricky part is GPT-Live can delegate mid-sentence before the user finishes speaking, so a tiny gap doesn't always mean continuation, and delaying every claim to wait for stragglers would hurt latency. The more targeted fix is to only apply that contiguous-gap check to leftover fragments that arrive right after a hand-off point.

content.text:
Saying "Stop, go to the next one" while Moneo is speaking a result now works, and I simplified the call logic, all in commit `d5f56035`. It's one commit rather than two, because both changes touch the same few lines. Unit tests (1200) and lint pass, and the real call check passes all 12 of its checks.

**Stop and move to the next result.** I tested this live: I asked two questions, said "Stop, go to the next one" partway through the first answer, and Moneo:
- stopped the first answer and didn't come back to it,
- went straight on to the second answer,
- didn't run "stop, go to the next one" as a request of its own.

Before, it told the voice model to judge for itself whether you'd asked it to stop. Now the app checks your words for "stop", "skip", "enough", "never mind", "forget it", "move on", "next one/result/answer" or German "stopp/weiter/nächste", and drops the result when you do. That only applies to short phrases of up to 8 words, so "what about next month?" or a longer question that happens to contain "stop" still runs as a normal request. A short "mm-hm" still doesn't count as an interruption.

**Over-engineering removed** (121 lines deleted, 42 added in the call controller and its tests):
- **Word-guessing rules removed.** They tried to spot requests the voice said yes to but never handed over. Requests now come only from hand-offs and typed messages. The cost: if the voice model agrees to something without handing it over, that request is lost instead of being guessed. It didn't happen in either live test.
- **Duplicate "still working" message merged.** Running tasks are now announced only once, after about 8 seconds and only when nobody is talking.
- **Kept on purpose: the server's one-line "also/too" check**, which stops a request like "also do last month" from cancelling the one before it. It's a cheap safeguard against a wrong cancel, not complexity.

**Known issue, not fixed:** in one live run the voice model handed over "How much did I spend at Netto this" before the last word, so "month" was attached to the start of the next request. The old code would have done the same, since it depends on when the hand-off arrives; the first run split the requests correctly. Fixing it would mean waiting about a second before starting every request, so I left it for you to decide.

I notice the early hand-off consistently drops the last word of the transcript, like "last" getting cut from "last month" or "Starbucks" from "today" — it's systematic, since GPT-Live's offset lands before the final word. This needs fixing since it corrupts requests; maybe I should wait for the transcript to settle, deferring the claim until the user's been quiet for around 700ms and including pieces that start before offset plus some grace period.

But grace alone feels fragile — I'd rather claim words up through the offset plus any immediately contiguous leftover pieces based on timing, where a piece counts if its start is close enough to the end of the last claimed piece. I need actual raw timing data to calibrate this, which means logging delegation offsets against word start times, so I should modify the run script to dump these raw lines to a file for inspection.

Separately, there's a bug where correcting an expense still spoke the replaced result — the original task finished and handed over its result before the replacement call could suppress it, since replaced() only drops queued tasks, not ones already in flight. The card was correctly dismissed server-side, but the voice output still referenced the old amount, which seems like an unavoidable race unless I can hook in earlier.

For small talk and the "still working" duplicate announcements, I'm noting these as minor/acceptable, though I could simplify the stalled-task announcer to batch all unannounced running tasks together rather than firing separately. I'll prioritize fixing the word-claiming timing issue first and gather the raw data needed.

content.thinking:
Expensefix is fixed now, showing only 15 cards. But testing the correction flow reveals a regression: when the user said "No wait, I meant this month," GPT-Live just said "checking this month" without actually handing off the request, so it got lost — exactly the kind of case the removed heuristics used to catch. I need a simple, non-heuristic fallback for when GPT-Live claims it's handling something but leaves it unclaimed.

One option: if words go unclaimed after the user stops talking and no hand-off arrives within N seconds, start them as a request — but that risks misfiring on small talk like "hey how are you," which would get treated as a real request and awkwardly answered by the chat model. A compromise rule of requiring 3+ words and 4 seconds of silence still fails on short greetings. Maybe the better fix is to have the chat model itself detect pure small talk and respond with a sentinel like "NO_REQUEST" so the controller knows not to speak it — a cleaner, deterministic solution than word-count heuristics.

I'm now sketching the implementation: after unclaimed-quiet timeout, if heard words ≥3 and not a skip phrase, start the task with an `unprompted: true` context flag. The server prompt gets an added instruction telling it to reply exactly "NONE" if the words are only small talk needing no answer, and the controller then drops/removes any task whose result is "NONE" so it never flashes in the UI. I also need to handle delegation ID for speaking results when there's no prior delegation, probably falling back to null with adjusted wording.

Weighing the complexity against what the user actually wants (removing over-engineering, testing), I think the pragmatic path is to restore the simpler of the two heuristics — claimUnheard plus the looksLikeRequest regex check — since that's what caught the quiet-4s case that got missed. I'll skip restoring the more fragile claimTakenOn logic and pull the relevant pieces back via git history.

content.thinking:
Requests are now correct, but there's still a timing issue: the old result gets spoken before a correction can replace it, since the replace tool only runs after the old request completes and hands off. I'm considering whether to hold a result from being spoken until I can confirm no newer correcting request is already underway, but detecting that in time is tricky.

A workable rule: if a newer task has started and is still deciding its first step (hasn't yet called a tool), wait up to ~4 seconds before releasing the earlier result, since it might get replaced. I'd implement this by tracking a `startedAt` timestamp per task and checking it during flush, bounded by that timeout window. Looking at the actual run, the old result was indeed handed off after the correction had already begun, so this rule should fix that case.

content.thinking:
For s1's correction, GPT-Live said "I'll check that too" which matches the TAKES_ON pattern, but no chat session seems to have started for it despite the 50-second run — the "started words" weren't logged. I suspect this is because claimTakenOn requires the time since last user speech to be at least 2000ms at the check point, scheduled 2s after reply start, so if the user's transcript arrived after the reply began, the timing condition could fail.

I need to fix this so the check retries while the user keeps talking: if the user spoke recently, reschedule the check instead of giving up, with a 500ms delay before trying again. This should still stop cleanly if delegation arrives and the heard words drop below the threshold.

I also need to address the two failing tests — they're cut-off tests where d3 is missing a step, so I should add tool events for d3 in those tests at the second ask index.

I think I should hold results when GPT-Live has pending unclaimed words it's taken on, so mayBeReplaced should also be true if there's a takenOn value with heard words present, bounded by claimTaken.

git add lib/ai/voice-call.ts app/api/chat/route.ts app/api/chat/route.test.ts && git commit -q -m "Let a call correction replace the last answered request, not only a running one

\"Actually make it fifteen\" after the first card was made left both cards on screen, because a
finished request was no longer offered to call_replace_task. The call brief now carries answered
requests' ids, and with none running the last answered one can be replaced (its cards dismissed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git add lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts lib/ai/voice-call-controller.test.ts && git commit -q -m "Keep the user's last word in call requests, and don't say an answer a correction replaces

Found testing calls with real speech:
- GPT-Live's hand-off offset points at the start of the user's last word, so it was cut off into
  the next request (\"groceries last\" / \"month No wait…\"). Words starting at the offset now belong
  to it, and a hand-off that arrives before the transcript catches up waits for it.
- A correction GPT-Live said it was on but never handed off was lost; once GPT-Live says it is on
  something and the words stay unclaimed while the user is quiet, they start as a request.
- An answer was said just before the correction that replaced it decided to; results now wait up to
  5 s for a later request's first step, or for words GPT-Live took on to start.
- \">\" break marks are left out of requests like \"|\".
